chapter: The New Orleans Owls and their members
title: Trombone, bass and tuba with the Owls; Dan LeBlanc
summary: Netto says he did not play tuba with the Owls, tells what became of Dan LeBlanc, mentions playing bass with Almerico on a boat during the war, and says his trombone was stolen.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you play any tuba with the owls ever? No. You didn't? No, no. Did you play string bass with the owls at the same time when Dan LeBlanc was around playing tuba?

No, no. I was on some bone now. And Dan, when the orchestra broke up, Dan went to school. He went to Loyola and became a teacher. Became a teacher? Yeah. He played too, he played too. What did he teach? Do you remember? He taught in St. Bernard Parish. He taught at school and the system there. Music? Yeah, he taught music. And I could never stand Lou Wap, why he didn't give him a job, with all of these funny yokels they had, you know, around there that he put on. And of course, Lou Wap, I don't want to say that. He's not one of my favorites. Did you ever play with him? Many of them. Not many, not many. I played for Stan Bow, you know, when Dick was there to take a night off, I played with him. He shoveled, you know, he shoveled it up there at what Truman calls fertilizer. You know, he'd throw it up there and throw it at you. And I told him, I said, I've made all of that before.
You played with Tony Amarico in that band. You played with him some other times too, didn't you?
Oh yeah, I played with Tony quite a while. On a boat at the Capitol during the war. Tony had a fine band on that boat.
And you played trombone with him or bass? No, no, I was on bass. You were on bass.
Trombone. Somebody stole the trombone. Somebody probably heard me play it and just stole it.
When did you stop playing trombone?
At the end of the owls? At the end of the owls, yeah. And you haven't played it since? No, I never did.
